changes: Run Moku v4 on the rectified board and on four overlapping crops, so dense boards are not truncated by the 300-detection limit
Refit the 19 x 19 lattice to detected stone centres, because stones sit above the board plane
Reject detections narrower than 0.89 of the median confident stone width (stickers and markers)
Check each candidate's pixels against black, white and empty-board colours sampled from nearby points in the same photo
Count a tall stone seen at an angle once, not again on the neighbouring point
If corner detection fails, merge corner peaks from a mirrored pass and retry
Return review points (overruled, borderline or duplicate candidates); the page outlines them for checking

references.source: User-supplied screenshots from a separate paid recognition tool, one per real photo; the user confirmed these positions are correct
references.orientation: Each reference was rotated or mirrored once to the photo's upright orientation before scoring

method.upload: Same as the page: longest edge up to 3072 pixels, JPEG quality 0.88, reduced by 0.8 until at most 1,050,000 bytes
method.conditionNote: Synthetic changes to the same four photos: resizing, brightness, contrast, colour cast, uneven lighting, blur, rotation and heavier JPEG compression. They test robustness, not new board positions.
method.machine: Local Apple Silicon CPU, ONNX Runtime with THREADS=1; excludes upload and Lambda start-up

remainingErrors: Photo 2 under darker or lower-contrast conditions: a white sticker at the left edge read as one or two white stones
Photo 4 under glare, blur or a blue cast: one or two extra white stones on empty points in the lower middle
caveats: The thresholds were developed on these same four photos; the augmented conditions reduce, but do not remove, the risk of overfitting
Four photos do not establish general real-world accuracy. Held-out photos with independent reference positions are needed
Users must still compare the board with the photo before analysis
